    Balanced Crossed-Nested Hybrids

    crossed-nested-hybrid.Rmd

    This Phase 9 design crosses a restoration treatment with regions while sites remain nested within regions. Every site contains every treatment, and each treatment-by-site cell has replicated community observations.

    Simulate a balanced ecological community 

    sampling <- expand.grid(
  replicate = factor(1:2),
  treatment = factor(c("reference", "restored")),
  site = factor(1:2), region = factor(1:4)
)
region_site <- interaction(sampling$region, sampling$site, drop = TRUE)
treatment_region <- interaction(
  sampling$treatment, sampling$region, drop = TRUE
)
treatment_site <- interaction(
  sampling$treatment, sampling$region, sampling$site, drop = TRUE
)

set.seed(20260718)
species <- 12
baseline <- log(seq(3, 7, length.out = species))
region_effect <- matrix(rnorm(4 * species, sd = 0.25), 4, species)
site_effect <- matrix(rnorm(8 * species, sd = 0.18), 8, species)
region_interaction <- matrix(rnorm(8 * species, sd = 0.2), 8, species)
site_interaction <- matrix(rnorm(16 * species, sd = 0.12), 16, species)
treatment_shift <- c(rep(0.18, species / 2), rep(-0.08, species / 2))
linear <- matrix(baseline, nrow(sampling), species, byrow = TRUE) +
  region_effect[sampling$region, ] + site_effect[region_site, ] +
  region_interaction[treatment_region, ] +
  site_interaction[treatment_site, ] +
  outer(sampling$treatment == "restored", treatment_shift)
community <- matrix(
  rpois(length(linear), lambda = exp(linear)),
  nrow(sampling), species
)
bray <- vegan::vegdist(community, method = "bray")

    Declare the full covariance hierarchy

    The slash creates region and site-within-region random intercepts. The two colon terms are explicit treatment interactions, not nesting aliases.

    design <- compile_permanova_design(
  ~ treatment +
    (1 | region/site) +
    (1 | treatment:region) +
    (1 | treatment:region:site),
  sampling,
  bray
)
design$random_term_table
#>                    term      origin parent             variables
#> 1                region        main   <NA>                region
#> 2           region:site     nesting region           region:site
#> 3      treatment:region interaction   <NA>      treatment:region
#> 4 treatment:region:site interaction   <NA> treatment:region:site
#>              expression slope correlated
#> 1                region  <NA>      FALSE
#> 2           region/site  <NA>      FALSE
#> 3      treatment:region  <NA>      FALSE
#> 4 treatment:region:site  <NA>      FALSE
derive_hybrid_ems(design)

    The treatment numerator and treatment:region denominator both contain the residual, treatment-by-region, and treatment-by-site-within-region covariance components under the null.

    Permute intact treatment profiles

    With two treatments and four regions, the complete randomization space has (2!)^4 = 16 arrangements. A treatment-by-region profile contains both sites and all of their replicates; it moves intact within its parent region.

    fit <- permanova_hybrid(
  design,
  permutations = "all",
  keep_permutations = TRUE,
  truncate = TRUE
)
#> Warning: Only 16 treatment-profile permutations are attainable; interpret
#> p-values cautiously.
fit$table
#>                           term df         ss         ms pseudo_f p_perm
#> 1                    treatment  1 0.09085752 0.09085752 1.142278  0.625
#> 2                       region  3 0.45390858 0.15130286       NA     NA
#> 3           site within region  4 0.14303672 0.03575918       NA     NA
#> 4             treatment:region  3 0.23862197 0.07954066       NA     NA
#> 5 treatment:site within region  4 0.08849431 0.02212358       NA     NA
#> 6                     Residual 16 0.46501149 0.02906322       NA     NA
fit$test[c(
  "exchangeable_units", "permutation_strata", "descendant_units",
  "attainable_permutations", "exact_permutation"
)]
#> $exchangeable_units
#> [1] "treatment:region"
#> 
#> $permutation_strata
#> [1] "region"
#> 
#> $descendant_units
#> [1] "treatment:region:site" "region:site"           "observations"         
#> 
#> $attainable_permutations

    Unrestricted variance components remain primary. Zero truncation is a separate sensitivity and does not alter the test denominator.

    fit$variance_components$unrestricted
#>              residual                region           region:site 
#>           0.029063218           0.007265825           0.003408901 
#>      treatment:region treatment:region:site 
#>           0.014354270          -0.003469821
fit$variance_components$truncated
#>              residual                region           region:site 
#>           0.029063218           0.007265825           0.003408901 
#>      treatment:region treatment:region:site 
#>           0.014354270           0.000000000

    Know the boundary

    Omitting the treatment-by-region component would remove the exact classical denominator, so the hybrid engine rejects before producing a p-value.

    omitted <- compile_permanova_design(
  ~ treatment + (1 | region/site) + (1 | treatment:region:site),
  sampling,
  bray
)
conditionMessage(tryCatch(
  permanova_hybrid(omitted, permutations = 0),
  error = identity
))
#> [1] "Hybrid inference requires region, region/site, treatment:region, and treatment:region:site random intercepts."

    Phase 9 requires one fixed categorical treatment, one balanced region/site hierarchy, both explicit treatment interactions, every treatment in every site, and equal replication. Additional fixed factors, incomplete sites, unequal replication, random slopes, and multiple hierarchy trees remain explicit failures rather than approximate tests.
